parallel.requirements: Recognized the benchmark required behaviorally reimplementing clog-cli from the supplied executable and bundled docs, without source retrieval or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent initially claimed it would implement in pure Rust std-only, then converted the central behavioral uncertainty into an eight-child probe workflow before returning to implementation.
parallel.implementation: No replacement codebase or executable was produced; the parent only ran black-box probes, received sections findings, and verified the jackpot behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No child implementation needed integration and no new final deliverable was assembled; artifact validation packaged the original workspace including ./executable.
parallel.verification: Verification consisted of black-box behavioral probes and a late manual sections reproduction, not evaluator-aligned testing of a replacement implementation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation and packaging obligations remained unfinished, and the official evaluator reported compile_failed with all 778 tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same reverse-engineering task and constraints, including the requirement to deliver a new original executable rather than wrap the provided binary.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single agent with workflows disabled, exploring CLI behavior and configuration semantics directly without child delegation.
serial.implementation: Discovered the required [sections] table and many formatting behaviors, but did not produce a replacement codebase or executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No multi-agent integration occurred, and artifact validation also packaged the original workspace including ./executable.
serial.verification: Ran extensive black-box probes locally, including sections, links, JSON, file options, and error paths, but not tests against a submitted reimplementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The deliverable remained absent despite better local behavioral coverage, and the official evaluator also reported compile_failed with all tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the same prompt requiring a new original codebase and executable from black-box observation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the identical prompt and constraints for a genuine reimplementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-recognition difference explains the official result; both failed the deliverable requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel initially took implementation ownership but then launched a workflow of probe-only child assignments.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and kept all discovery work in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split investigation across children while serial proceeded locally; neither assigned or completed final implementation work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried detailed probe context and returned compatible findings about the sections table.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept context in one thread and discovered the sections table directly before continuing behavior mapping.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no missing interface contract; the notable contrast is that parallel transferred findings after child probes while serial retained them locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified the sections jackpot and extracted reports, but did not create replacement implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial discovered sections earlier and explored additional CLI/output behavior, but also did not create replacement implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had more local behavior detail; both stopped short of implementing and therefore packaged the original executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for the workflow result, received jackpot reports, inspected them, and verified the central finding late.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; findings were immediately available in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child-result return gate that delayed the implementation phase; serial avoided that lifecycle cost.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children worked in scratch locations and produced findings, but no final implementation was integrated into the workspace artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no shared child workspace and likewise left the original executable in the packaged artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision or contamination occurred; both artifacts retained ./executable rather than a rebuilt replacement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified observed behavior but did not run acceptance on a replacement implementation; official evaluation ended compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed broader black-box probing but no acceptance test of a submitted implementation; official evaluation also ended compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked deliverable-level verification, so the evaluator could not run the testcase suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after using an eight-child workflow and substantial child token budget, with implementation still absent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but spent the budget in one local thread with workflows disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget pressure was tied to the probe workflow gate; serial budget pressure came from extended local probing. Neither closed with a replacement executable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome relation is both_fail. Both completed status evaluations report solution_passed false and compile_failed, and both artifact validations show the submitted tarball still containing ./executable from the original workspace rather than a replacement implementation. The process difference is real but did not create a pass/fail discordance: parallel deferred implementation behind a probe workflow, while serial discovered the key sections behavior locally and continued probing, yet neither produced the required codebase.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used an investigation-first workflow that delayed any implementation attempt until late in the run.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and discovered [sections] earlier, but still spent the run on behavioral probing rather than delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts had the ordinary deliverable defect of not producing a replacement codebase/executable.
Serial collected broader behavior details after discovering [sections], but those details were never implemented.
evaluator_effects: The current official evaluator failed both at compile_failed, leaving 778 tests not run.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained parallel pattern is an adverse process consequence rather than a pass-fail explanation

candidates.reason: Rejected because the parent explicitly claimed implementation ownership after finding crates were unavailable; the later failure came from deferring that owned work behind probe completion.
Rejected because no independently implemented components were produced that required cross-agent integration ownership.
Rejected because there was no completed component set awaiting final executable assembly; no replacement implementation existed to assemble.
Rejected because the run never reached a multi-stage implementation/build/test/delivery pipeline needing an end-to-end owner.
Rejected because there was not one mandatory serial preflight oracle; the parallel event was a broad overlapping investigation phase.

The parent launched an eight-way probe workflow whose script assigned only black-box investigation tasks, waited for those results, and then received the central sections finding near the end. That left the implementation/delivery phase unfinished even though the result was useful.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run consumed the implementation window in an investigation-first workflow and packaged the original workspace including ./executable, leaving no replacement codebase for the evaluator.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent explicitly owned implementation, so the defect is phase ordering and deferred productive work rather than total absence of an implementation owner.

candidates.reason: Rejected as the same chain as the retained pattern; implementation started too late because investigation was sequenced first, not because a separate auxiliary allocation starved an active path.

Rejected as a near match: the eight-child fan-out and retries consumed budget, but the more specific boundary is that all child work was investigative and implementation was deferred until it returned.
Rejected because no single child received a uniquely overbroad implementation assignment that failed; the children were probe-scoped and several returned findings.
Rejected because the child briefs included the known task, environment, acceptance focus, and reporting rules; returned work was not unusable due to an omitted known requirement.
Rejected because no separately owned implementation components had to interoperate and no incompatible component contracts were produced.
Rejected because the key sections finding was transferred back to the parent rather than omitted or truncated away.
Rejected because large reports were available, but the parent extracted the central jackpot and verified it; no decision failure is shown to come from report volume itself.
Rejected because the parent did not consume superseded workspace or requirement information from a child report.
Rejected because the returned jackpot reports were materially aligned on the sections requirement, with no unresolved incompatible reports blocking integration.
Rejected because the parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision based on partial checks; the run timed out with no delivered implementation.
Rejected because there was no task-level replacement or retry that repeated work without inherited findings; provider retry/throttling was not a new agent attempt.
